newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai shares edge up at noon despite crackdown.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai shares edge up at noon despite crackdown.

text.p: Shanghai shares edged up at midday on Friday despite Beijing's punishment of a string of major firms for illegal trading, but brokers said the news had been largely digested after weeks of swirling rumours.
Institutional buying aimed at stabilising the indices also contributed to the slight rise in the morning, brokers said.

The A share index gained 3.351 points or 0.28 percent to 1,269.369 on volume of 195.5 million shares worth 2.5 billion yuan. The B share index added 0.156 points or 0.19 percent to 83.074 on volume of 7.1 million shares worth $4.9 million.

China's regulators on Thursday announced punishment of a string of major listed firms and brokerages including the Shenzhen Development Bank Co and Shenyin & Wanguo Securities for illegal trading on the stock markets.

The announcement was another blow to market sentiment and the latest in the series of measures imposed by Beijing since early May to cool down stock trading, including banning state banks from trading on the stock markets, brokers said.
But rumours about the punishment had been circulating on the market for a long time and had been partly digested, they said.

"With the news out of the way, some investors began to build positions believing the indices have touched bottom after the falls of the past few days," said one broker. "Institutional window-dressing buying also helped the index to stabilise."

"Despite the rise in the morning, the announcement indicates the central government believes the stock markets are still too speculative," said a second broker. "If the markets rise solidly in the near future, the central government will possibly take Brokers said they expected the indices to consolidate in the short term.
On the B share market, Shanghai Jinqiao Export Processing Zone Development Co was the star performer on institutional buying, rising $0.034 or 4.22 percent to $0.838 on volume of 913,300 shares.

Market barometer Shanghai Lujiazui Finance Trade Zone Development Co was the most actively traded also on institutional support, gaining $0.610 or 0.71 percent to $0.838 on volume of 1.1 million shares.
On the A share market, the SSE 30 blue-chip index gained 16.850 points or 0.45 percent to 3743.490 points.
Speculative stock Shenma Industry was the star performer on institutional window-dressing buying, jumping 0.93 yuan or 7.19 percent to 13.85 yuan on volume of 2.9 million shares.
